target.notes: Chakra UI v3, mounted with default configuration using only components the library exports and no hand-written ARIA. Chakra v3 is built on Ark UI, so these results describe that underlying behaviour as Chakra ships it.

assertions.title: Each header control sits inside a heading
assertions.rationale: Screen reader users navigate documents by heading. If accordion headers are not headings, an entire page structure disappears from the shortcut that most users rely on to move around it.
assertions.detail: One or more header controls are not contained in a heading.
assertions.expected: each control inside an h1–h6 or role=heading element
assertions.actual: hr-header-1, hr-header-2, hr-header-3 have no heading ancestor

assertions.title: Each header control exposes role=button
assertions.rationale: The control that expands a section must be announced as a button, or the user is not told it can be operated at all.
assertions.detail: All three header controls expose role=button.

assertions.title: Each header control has an accessible name
assertions.rationale: An unnamed control cannot be chosen deliberately from a list of them.
assertions.detail: All three headers expose their label.

assertions.title: Collapsed sections expose aria-expanded=false
assertions.rationale: Without it the user is not told the control expands anything, so a collapsed accordion reads as a list of inert buttons.
assertions.detail: All three sections report themselves collapsed.

assertions.title: The header control references its panel with aria-controls
assertions.rationale: The relationship is what lets assistive technology move from the control to the content it reveals.
assertions.detail: aria-controls references an element with id="accordion::r0::content:shipping"

assertions.title: Collapsed panels are hidden from assistive technology
assertions.rationale: A sighted user sees nothing. If the content is still in the accessibility tree, a screen reader user reads sections that appear closed, with no way to tell where one ends and the next begins.

assertions.title: Enter expands the focused section
assertions.rationale: The primary activation key. Without it the content is unreachable by keyboard.

assertions.title: Space expands the focused section
assertions.rationale: The APG requires both Enter and Space on the header. Space is routinely missed by implementations that attach a click handler to a non-button element.

assertions.title: An expanded panel is exposed and reveals its content
assertions.rationale: A header reporting itself expanded while its content stays hidden from assistive technology is worse than one that does nothing, because the announcement and the reality disagree.

assertions.title: Tab moves between accordion headers
assertions.rationale: Accordion headers are each a stop in the tab sequence, the opposite of a tablist, which is a single stop navigated with arrows. Implementations that copy tab behaviour here strand the user on the first header.

assertions.title: Activating an expanded header collapses it
assertions.rationale: A section that opens and cannot be closed leaves the user unable to get back to a scannable list, which is the whole reason for using an accordion.
